arxiv-2102-11011.title: The Uncanny Similarity of Recurrence and Depth
arxiv-2102-11011.creator: Avi Schwarzschild, Arjun Gupta, Amin Ghiasi, Micah Goldblum, Tom Goldstein
arxiv-2102-11011.description: Abstract It is widely believed that deep neural networks contain layer specialization, wherein neural networks extract hierarchical features representing edges and patterns in shallow layers and complete objects in deeper layers. Unlike common feed-forward models that have distinct filters at each layer, recurrent networks reuse the same parameters at various depths.

arxiv-2105-02386.title: Automated Primary Hyperparathyroidism Screening with Neural Networks
arxiv-2105-02386.creator: Noah Ziems, Shaoen Wu, Jim Norman
arxiv-2105-02386.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Noah Ziems, Shaoen Wu, Jim Norman. Primary Hyperparathyroidism(PHPT) is a relatively common disease, affecting about one in every 1,000 adults. However, screening for PHPT can be difficult, meaning it often goes undiagnosed for long periods of time. While looking at specific blood test results independently can help indicate whether a patient has PHPT, often these blood result levels can all be within their respective normal ranges despite the patient having PHPT.

arxiv-2203-02549.title: Structured Pruning is All You Need for Pruning CNNs at Initialization
arxiv-2203-02549.creator: Yaohui Cai, Weizhe Hua, Hongzheng Chen
arxiv-2203-02549.description: Abstract Pruning-at-initialization (PAI) proposes to prune the individual weights of the CNN before training, thus avoiding expensive fine-tuning or retraining of the pruned model. While PAI shows promising results in reducing model size, the pruned model still requires unstructured sparse matrix computation, making it difficult to achieve wall-clock speedups.

arxiv-2207-01504.title: Can Population-based Engagement Improve Personalisation? A Novel Dataset and Experiments
arxiv-2207-01504.creator: Sahan Bulathwela 1, Meghana Verma 2, María Pérez-Ortiz 1, Emine Yilmaz 1 and John Shawe-Taylor 1
arxiv-2207-01504.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sahan Bulathwela 1, Meghana Verma 2, María Pérez-Ortiz 1, Emine Yilmaz 1 and John Shawe-Taylor 1. This work explores how population-based engagement prediction can address cold-start at scale in large learning resource collections. Forman, Christine Jones, Ildar Khabibullin, Caroline Kilbourne, Ralph Kraft, Erwin T. Lau, Sheng-Chieh Lin, Da
arxiv-2310-02225.description: Abstract High-resolution spectroscopy in soft X-rays will open a new window to map multiphase gas in galaxy clusters and probe physics of the intracluster medium (ICM), including chemical enrichment histories, circulation of matter and energy during large-scale structure evolution, stellar and black hole feedback, halo virialization, and gas mixing processes.

arxiv-2404-02438.title: From Narratives to Numbers: Valid Inference Using Language Model Predictions from Verbal Autopsy Narratives
arxiv-2404-02438.creator: Shuxian Fan, Adam Visokay *, Kentaro Hoffman, Stephen Salerno, Li Liu, Jeffrey T. Leek, Tyler H. McCormick
arxiv-2404-02438.description: Abstract In settings where most deaths occur outside the healthcare system, verbal autopsies (VAs) are a common tool to monitor trends in causes of death (COD). VAs are interviews with a surviving caregiver or relative that are used to predict the decedent’s COD.

arxiv-2410-22729.title: Identifying Drift, Diffusion, and Causal Structure from Temporal Snapshots
arxiv-2410-22729.creator: Vincent Guan vguan23@math.ubc.ca, Joseph Janssen joejanssen@eoas.ubc.ca, Hossein Rahmani hrahmani@math.ubc.ca, Andrew Warren awarren@math.ubc.ca, Stephen Y. Zhang syz@syz.id.au, Elina Robeva erobeva@math.ubc.ca, Geoffrey Schiebinger geoff@math.ubc.ca
arxiv-2410-22729.description: Abstract Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) are a fundamental tool for modelling dynamic processes, including gene regulatory networks (GRNs), contaminant transport, financial markets, and image generation. However, learning the underlying SDE from data is a challenging task, especially if individual trajectories are not observable.

pmc-10595235.title: Educational inequality in cause-specific mortality among immigrants and their descendants in Sweden
pmc-10595235.creator: A Miething
pmc-10595235.description: IntroductionAlthough immigrants in Western countries often face disadvantages and vulnerabilities such as lower socioeconomic status, they tend to exhibit weaker educational gradients in mortality compared to the native majority populations. However, it is unclear how these gradients vary across specific causes of death and whether they persist among second-generation immigrants.

pmc-10638811.title: Care pathways of sepsis survivors: sequelae, mortality and use of healthcare services in France, 2015–2018
pmc-10638811.creator: Fanny Pandolfi, Christian Brun-Buisson, Didier Guillemot, Laurence Watier
pmc-10638811.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundIndividuals who survive sepsis are at high risk of chronic sequelae, resulting in significant health-economic costs. Several studies have focused on aspects of healthcare pathways of sepsis survivors but comprehensive, longitudinal overview of their pathways of care are scarce.

pmc-11644848.title: Automated Detection of Gastrointestinal Diseases Using Resnet50*-Based Explainable Deep Feature Engineering Model with Endoscopy Images
pmc-11644848.creator: Veysel Yusuf Cambay, Prabal Datta Barua, Abdul Hafeez Baig, Sengul Dogan, Mehmet Baygin, Turker Tuncer, U R Acharya, Stefanos Kollias
pmc-11644848.description: This work aims to develop a novel convolutional neural network (CNN) named ResNet50* to detect various gastrointestinal diseases using a new ResNet50*-based deep feature engineering model with endoscopy images. The novelty of this work is the development of ResNet50*, a new variant of the ResNet model, featuring convolution-based residual blocks and a pooling-based attention mechanism similar to PoolFormer.

pmc-12508077.title: Effectiveness and durability of a fourth dose of ancestral-strain mRNA vaccines against SARS-CoV-2 infection: a nationwide matched cohort study in Qatar
pmc-12508077.creator: Layan Sukik, Hiam Chemaitelly, Houssein H. Ayoub, Peter Coyle, Patrick Tang, Mohammad R. Hasan, Hadi M. Yassine, Asmaa A. Al Thani, Zaina Al-Kanaani, Einas Al-Kuwari, Andrew Jeremijenko, Anvar Hassan Kaleeckal, Ali Nizar Latif, Riyazuddin Mohammad Shaik, Hanan F. Abdul-Rahim, Gheyath K. Nasrallah, M
pmc-12508077.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Concerns about waning immunity against severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection and the emergence of new variants underscore the need for booster doses. Using a matched cohort design, this study evaluated the relative effectiveness and durability of a fourth dose of ancestral-strain mRNA vaccines (BNT162b2 or mRNA-1273) in preventing SARS-CoV-2 infection, compared to three doses, between February 10, 2021 and May 13, 2024 in Qatar.

For these farmers, weighing scales are not readily accessible; hence, sales of sheep are mostly dependent on physical appearance.

pmc-12951307.creator: Mariana Hoffman, Simone Dal Corso, Jean Bremner, Anne E. Holland
pmc-12951307.description: BackgroundClinical trials are the best method for evaluating new treatments for people with interstitial lung disease (ILD). However, recruitment in ILD clinical trials is often challenging. Certain trial characteristics may influence willingness to participate but this has not been investigated in people with ILD.

pmc-13361743.description: BackgroundIncreasing same-day placement rates of long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARCs) for individuals who are medically eligible and desire to do so is a key component of contraceptive access. pmc-13608987.title: Growth-Phase-Dependent Shift in GABA Biosynthetic Pathways Under Temperature Stress in Isochrysis zhanjiangensis
pmc-13608987.creator: Jiansen Luo, Lin Zhang, Jichang Han, Yumeng Wang, Jiaxin Yu, Jingbo Fan, Lulu Wang, Jiayi Cao, Kehou Pan, Jilin Xu
pmc-13608987.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Temperature stress is a major constraint on the productivity of microalgae used in aquaculture. γ-Aminobutyric acid (GABA) is well-established as a key player in the stress tolerance of higher plants, yet its role in microalgae remains largely unexplored. Here, we examined the effects of low (15 °C), optimal (25 °C), and high (35 °C) temperatures on the GABA shunt in Isochrysis zhanjiangensis during the initial and mid-exponential growth phases.
